key_insight: Bioconvection from motile microorganisms can create self-organized convective plumes that enhance heat and mass transfer with little or no mechanical pumping.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a low-carbon, bio-inspired route to improve thermal management efficiency in data centers, electronics, and other high-heat systems.
method: Review and synthesize studies from natural ecosystems and lab experiments on microorganism-induced flow.
Analyze pattern formation, hydrodynamics, and thermofluidic transport in bioconvective systems.
Use non-dimensional numbers and quantitative thermal-performance comparisons to assess feasibility.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative analyses of thermal performance and framework-based evaluation using relevant non-dimensional numbers, rather than a single new experiment.
watch_item: Practical deployment is still constrained by microbial stability, material compatibility, controllability, scalability, and integration with existing cooling hardware.
paper_title: Engineering Collective Microbial Dynamics for Sustainable Thermal Management
